topic: What if you could teleport just by blinking?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
TELEPORT BY BLINKING?

power.rule: shut your eyes, picture a place, open them and you're there; you keep whatever speed you had
power.look: Pip shrinks into a cyan ring and a pinch of sparks where he stood, and pops in with a ring where he lands; a BLINK chip

script.text: Snack time. Blink. You're at the fridge.
Late for class. Blink. First one there.
Mo looks back. Blink. You're right behind him.
What if you could teleport by blinking?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: Earth spins. The equator moves at over sixteen hundred kilometres an hour. That's real.
Blink to the North Pole... and you keep that speed.

science.claim: The equator moves at over sixteen hundred kilometres an hour.
science.working: Earth's equatorial circumference is 40,075 km and it turns once every sidereal day, 23.934 h. 40,075 / 23.934 = 1,674 km/h (465 m/s). Over 1,600 holds.
science.source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet (equatorial radius 6,378.137 km, sidereal rotation period 23.9345 h)

science.claim: Blink to the North Pole and you keep that speed.
science.working: The episode's rule: a blink moves you but keeps your momentum (Newton's first law: nothing acts on you to slow you). At the pole the ground's rotational speed is 0, so you arrive moving about 1,674 km/h relative to the ice. The rule is the story's; the speed is real.
science.source: Newton's first law; NASA Earth Fact Sheet

shots.note: Pip at his desk, an empty plate with crumbs, looks off toward the door; hungry
BLINK: his eyes squeeze shut, then he shrinks into a cyan ring and a pinch of sparks
Pip pops in by the fridge with a cyan ring, grinning; the cat jolts awake on the counter
the alarm clock flips 08:59 to 09:00, red digits
BLINK: Pip in shock, bag strap on, eyes shut, gone in a ring
empty classroom; Pip pops in at his desk, first one there, smug
Mo halfway down the stairs looks back up over his shoulder: nobody there
BLINK: Pip's eyes shut at the top of the stairs, glint, gone
Mo turns forward and Pip is right behind him, inches away, grinning; Mo jolts
the premise over the dusk city; Pip pops onto the roof
a globe; cyan pins pop in all over it: anywhere
Pip's grin fades; he looks down
the globe turns, a curved arrow round it: EARTH SPINS
the equator draws on, a dot rides it with speed streaks
1,674 KM/H counts up big, OVER 1,600 under it
Pip, worried; the light turning red
Pip's dot hops from the equator to the North Pole; the pole reads 0 KM/H, Pip still 1,674
Pip pops onto the ice and is flung sideways out of frame at speed; snow spray, shake
